macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum edge higher while XRP and Dogecoin slip amid U.S. crypto bill standoff
items.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum traded modestly higher, while XRP and Dogecoin fell as markets tracked renewed Senate efforts to advance the CLARITY Act before recess. The report also noted more than $250 million in crypto liquidations over the prior 24 hours and a global market cap around $2.2 trillion.

items.title: Crypto market weakens as Bitcoin holds near $64,000 and Ethereum gains
items.summary: Major coins moved unevenly, with Bitcoin trading near $64,360, Ethereum rising about 1.8%, and XRP, Solana, BNB, TRON, Hyperliquid, and Dogecoin mostly lower. Coinglass data cited in the report showed roughly $241 million in liquidations over 24 hours, reflecting continued volatility.

items.title: U.S. crypto regulation debate continues as Senate pushes CLARITY Act
items.summary: Coverage from market reports said lawmakers renewed efforts to pass the CLARITY Act before the recess, highlighting that regulatory uncertainty is still influencing trading sentiment. Related commentary also noted concerns around stablecoin and market-structure rules in the broader policy debate.

items.title: Bank of England publishes stablecoin rules for UK issuers
items.summary: Investing.com reported new stablecoin rules from the Bank of England for UK issuers, adding to a growing set of regulatory measures affecting the sector. The same roundup also mentioned Fed proposals for customer ID rules for stablecoin issuers and a Singapore investor alert involving Bybit.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation cuts 20% of staff in sweeping restructure
items.summary: Investing.com highlighted a major internal restructuring at the Ethereum Foundation, including a 20% staff reduction. The move stands out as one of the most notable project-related developments in the past day.

items.title: Strategy sells MSTR shares and buys 520 bitcoins
items.summary: Investing.com reported that Strategy used an at-the-market share sale to buy an additional 520 bitcoins, reinforcing its continued accumulation strategy. The same roundup also said the company had disclosed fresh corporate activity around its Bitcoin holdings.

items.title: Bonzo Lend loses $9 million in Hedera oracle exploit
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported a $9 million exploit at Bonzo Lend tied to an oracle issue on Hedera. The incident adds to recent DeFi security concerns as attackers continue to target protocol infrastructure.

items.title: Robinhood says AI agent feature will soon assist crypto traders
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that Robinhood plans to add an AI agent feature for crypto traders soon, signaling another product expansion in retail trading tools. The development comes alongside broader competition among platforms for active crypto users.

items.title: LAB token collapses more than 85% in 24 hours
items.summary: Odaily reported that the LAB token fell from about $14 to under $2 in a single day, wiping out much of its valuation. The outlet said the fully diluted valuation also dropped sharply from around $14 billion.

items.title: EU considers expanding MiCA to cover tokenization and non-EU stablecoin issuers
items.summary: Odaily reported that the European Union is weighing amendments to broaden MiCA’s scope to include tokenization and stablecoin issuers outside the EU. If adopted, the change would expand the bloc’s already influential crypto rulebook.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 preview, new models Sol, Terra, and Luna
items.summary: OpenAI announced a limited preview of its GPT-5.6 model suite, including Sol, Terra, and Luna, amid ongoing U.S. AI regulatory scrutiny. The release is one of the biggest model-launch stories in the past day.

items.title: OpenAI reveals first in-house AI chip, Jalapeño
items.summary: OpenAI introduced its first AI processor, called Jalapeño, signaling a push to reduce dependence on Nvidia for large-scale inference workloads. The announcement adds to the growing trend of major AI firms designing custom silicon.

items.title: ChatGPT adds Getty Images photos through licensing deal
items.summary: OpenAI said ChatGPT will now surface licensed Getty Images content in responses and search results under a multi-year agreement. The deal reflects a broader push to secure premium content rights for AI products.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Image model for Instagram-integrated AI photos
items.summary: Meta’s new Muse image model can incorporate other Instagram users into AI-generated photos, raising privacy and consent questions. The launch highlights Meta’s expanding consumer AI push across its social platforms.

items.title: Meta prepares Muse video generator
items.summary: The Verge reported that Meta is planning to launch a Muse video generator next, extending its generative media strategy beyond images. This fits the wider industry trend toward multimodal consumer AI tools.

items.title: Google Photos adds AI video remix features
items.summary: Google Photos now lets users remix videos with AI effects such as cinematic relighting, custom backgrounds, watercolor, and sketch-style transformations. The rollout shows continued competition in creative AI editing tools.

items.title: Microsoft 365 favors its own AI models over ChatGPT and Claude
items.summary: PCMag reported that Microsoft 365 apps are increasingly prioritizing Microsoft’s own AI models instead of external ones like ChatGPT and Claude. The move suggests a broader platform strategy to internalize AI spend and control model usage.

items.title: Anthropic’s latest model gets broader release after safety review
items.summary: Ars Technica reported that Anthropic’s advanced Fable and Mythos models received a global release after earlier safety testing concerns. The story underscores how frontier model rollouts are increasingly tied to regulatory and safety scrutiny.

items.title: OpenAI and Broadcom announce chip designed for large-scale LLM inference
items.summary: Ars Technica reported that OpenAI and Broadcom jointly announced a chip aimed at large-language-model inference at scale. This is part of a growing wave of custom AI hardware development among leading model companies.

items.title: Nscale raises $900 million for AI data-center buildout
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia-backed startup Nscale secured $900 million to accelerate data-center expansion across Europe, the U.S., and Asia Pacific. The funding highlights continued investment surges in AI infrastructure.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Google loses final challenge to EU’s record antitrust fine
items.summary: Google lost its last legal bid to overturn the European Union’s record $4.7 billion antitrust fine, marking another major regulatory setback for Big Tech in Europe. The ruling reinforces the EU’s long-running crackdown on Google’s Android and advertising practices.

items.title: Microsoft cuts about 3,200 Xbox jobs in restructuring push
items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly laying off around 3,200 workers in its Xbox video game business as it restructures the division and redirects resources. The move is part of a broader effort to reshape its gaming operations.

items.title: Google sets Pixel 11 launch event for August 12
items.summary: Google has scheduled its Pixel 11 launch event for August 12, signaling the next major Android hardware announcement. Reports suggest the event could also bring possible price increases for some devices.

items.title: Amazon says its satellite network is ready for initial broadband service
items.summary: Amazon says it has enough satellites in orbit to begin initial broadband service at mid-latitudes later this year. The milestone advances its effort to compete in the satellite internet market.

items.title: Blue Origin expected to raise private capital at $130 billion valuation
items.summary: Blue Origin is reportedly preparing to raise private capital for the first time, with the company seeking around $10 billion. The fundraising would value the space company at roughly $130 billion.

items.title: FCC moves to end Biden-era broadband fee disclosure rule
items.summary: The FCC is set to let internet service providers stop itemizing passthrough fees and instead show a single 'up to' price. The change would reverse a Biden-era disclosure requirement that aimed to make internet pricing more transparent.

items.title: Adidas releases limited run of 3D-printed shoes
items.summary: Adidas is launching fewer than 200 pairs of its latest 3D-printed shoe, underscoring how experimental premium footwear remains. The release highlights continued interest in additive manufacturing for consumer products.
